requirement:
The `{term}` role followed by a backtick-delimited full definition name MUST reference a named definition. In rendered Markdown, the reference MUST display the definition's phrase as an ordinary hyperlink to its anchored declaration, without a badge. The phrase MUST be escaped appropriately for rendering.

Missing targets and targets of another kind MUST be reported. Escaped references and references in Markdown code examples MUST remain literal. A term reference MUST NOT satisfy a requirement citation or a Rust function's requirement-coverage obligation.
rationale: The implementation looks complete and correctly marked. One required failure case has no test, so I am not calling the requirement satisfied. **Implementation** - **Rendering.** `replace_inline_references` (src/lib.rs) turns `{term}` into `phrase`. It produces no badge and no class, and it resolves the link target with `chapter_href` and `DefinitionKind::anchor`. - **Escaping.** The phrase goes through `terms::escaped_phrase`, which turns Markdown-significant characters into numeric entities and HTML-escapes the rest. `replace_definitions` emits the matching anchored `` declaration. - **Literals.** `reference_roles` skips backslash-escaped roles (`is_escaped`) and roles in code spans, code blocks and HTML (`protected_ranges`), so they stay literal. It also protects the `:phrase:` option line of term declarations. When the target is missing or of another kind, the renderer leaves the text literal. - **Reporting.** `validate_references` (src/evidence.rs) reports `term X has no matching named definition` when a `{term}` target is missing or not a term. It reports `{impl|cite|test}`NAME` has no matching requirement or example` when the target is missing or is a term. - **No citation credit.** Term references are never added to `by_definition`, so they cannot satisfy a requirement citation or evidence coverage. `missing_function_references` (src/rust_coverage.rs) returns false for `ReferenceKind::Term`, so a term does not count as Rust item coverage. - **Marking.** `{impl}` markers are present on every relevant function I found (`ReferenceKind`, `label`, `color`, `anchor`, `preprocess_book`, `replace_definitions`, `replace_inline_references`, `reference_roles`, `referenced_terms`, `escaped_phrase`, `validate_references`, `missing_function_references`). I found no unmarked behaviour that belongs to this requirement. **Tests** - `phrases_are_plain_links_and_markdown_literals_are_preserved` checks that there is no shields.io badge, exactly one correct hyperlink, an escaped phrase, and that the inline-code, fenced-code and backslash-escaped forms stay literal. `a_term_reference_renders_only_its_phrase_as_a_plain_link` checks the exact output, with no markup beyond the one anchor. That second test carries only `phrase_rendering`, not this requirement. - `invalid_declarations_and_reference_targets_are_reported` checks a missing term target (`missing.name`) and a `{term}` that points at a requirement (`rules.ready`). - `definition_schema_deletion_and_literal_references_are_checked` checks that literal and escaped references, including ones to a missing name, raise no errors and add no dependencies. - `outline_inputs_capture_terms_without_counting_them_as_citations` checks that a function with only a `{term}` comment is reported as having no requirement or example citation. **Gap** - The "target of another kind" case for `{impl}`, `{cite}` and `{test}` pointing at a term definition goes through the `has no matching requirement or example` branch of `validate_references`. No test exercises it. The only tests I found for that message use missing names (`src/evidence.rs` `reports_unknown_references_and_uncovered_lines`, and `configuration_and_dependency_failures_do_not_stop_later_checks`). The term-to-example kind mismatch is also untested. - There is no FIXME or other source comment acknowledging this gap, so the result is `false` rather than `FIXME`.
